title: The Delhi Spectacle Gives Way to the Deegh Campaign

blocks.text: The closing motion of the Delhi episode lingers on imperial amazement at Sikh methods. The chronicler recalls gauhar ali patishah bhayo parsann dikh panth lut, using the emperor's pleasure at the staged plunder to underline how boldly the Khalsa could turn even mock disorder into political theater.

From there the narrative pivots southward. Jab khalso dakkhan chalyo mislain daso bani, the confederate misls move against Suraj Mal, and the remembered line jai suraj mal gheriyo dik ghumarhi mahi announces the struggle around Deegh and Ghumer as the next collective undertaking.

This damaged hinge page therefore does two jobs at once. It closes Baghel Singh's spectacular Delhi performance and opens the coordinated southern campaign that will lead into tribute, bargaining, and new internal questions about distribution.
